chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'I married a woman, and I found that a woman had breast-fed me and breast-fed her sister.' He said, 'How much?' I said, 'A little bit.' He said, 'May Allah bless you.'

key_terms.الْمَاضِي: The deceased / the late (referring to the 7th Imam Musa al-Kazim)
key_terms.شَيْئاً يَسِيراً: A little bit / a small amount

ai.seo_question: Does minor breast-feeding between a woman and her sister prohibit the sister from marrying the man who was breast-fed by the first woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'minor breast-feeding' (رضاع صغير), where the Imam confirms that a small amount of milk establishes kinship but does not prohibit marriage, as evidenced by the narrator's successful union. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the sufficiency of minimal nursing to create mahram relationships, distinguishing it from the more rigorous conditions often discussed in Sunni jurisprudence. The Imam’s concise response underscores the practical application of this rule in personal status law.
